notaTipos: Not a slip: they take different types. [iconDef] takes the icon's whole definition — its geometry plus its animation variants. [icon] takes the shape to morph INTO.
verEnApi: See both in the API reference →
notaSpring: spring takes a preset name. The full list, with the damping value behind each one, is in the API reference — it isn't copied here so the two can't drift apart.
intro: The icon grid shows what's there. This shows what it's for: controls that actually do what they say — the copy one copies, the theme one changes colors, the send one has its three states. Each one's code sits right next to it.

copiar.descripcion: The case where morph clearly wins: copy → check confirms without shifting the layout or bolting on a toast. The button above actually copies — try it and paste.
copiar.detalle: If writeText fails (no permission, no focus, site on http) the state doesn't change: the icon stays on copy instead of lying with a checkmark.

tema.descripcion: moon ↔ sun. The icon inherits the text color (stroke="currentColor"), so the theme never has to touch it directly: change the container's color and the icon follows.
tema.detalle: Here the theme only applies to this panel, so the pattern reads in isolation. The real one lives in the header, with the same morph: it writes data-tema on <html>, remembers your choice, and reveals the new theme with a circle that grows out of the button itself.

enviar.descripcion: Idle → sending → sent, and back again. send → circle-check via morph; the spinner is a curated <gf-icon> on loop.
enviar.detalle: Mixing them isn't sloppiness: a morph has a start and an end, and "loading" doesn't know when it's done. An unknown-duration state needs an animation that cycles — exactly what the choreography engine already does.

reaccion.descripcion: There's no morph here: the shape doesn't change, only the gesture. trigger="tap" replays the heart's curated choreography on every click, and the button supplies the color.
reaccion.detalle: The rule for picking an engine: if the icon changes shape, morph; if the same icon reacts, choreography. Using morph here would mean paying for the interpolation of two identical shapes.
